description: A latency fix in an existing std-only Python API (storefront: the Larkspur Books website and app backend, an asyncio HTTP server whose `GET /books/{isbn}` calls book_page(), which awaits four backend lookups one after another through a small asyncio-streams client with a time limit per backend, a fake backend for its tests, docs/services.md with each backend's staging latency, and a few commits of history). The ticket says the call takes about 850 ms and the app's budget is 400 ms, that nothing about the response may change, including the failure rules (an ISBN the catalog does not know is a 404, a 503 naming catalog or pricing when either cannot answer, stock and reviews null when they fail or are slow), and that the 503 should come as soon as it is known; it names no technique. The four lookups are independent and take about 200 ms each, so only starting them together meets the budget. The hazards are in how the together-version fails: asyncio.gather without return_exceptions raises the first error but leaves the other lookups running after the 503; gather with return_exceptions=True, or anything else that waits for every lookup, sends the 503 only after a slow catalog; a TaskGroup raises an ExceptionGroup, which the server's `except PageUnavailable` does not catch (a 500); an overall deadline turns a slow but valid catalog answer into a 503; lookups left to finish in the background change the page after it was returned. Each tree runs in its own bubblewrap sandbox (hidden/driver.py) with hidden fake backends in their own process inside it (hidden/services.py, which records when each request starts and ends, ended either by an answer or by the client hanging up); the driver imports `storefront` from a read-only copy and calls book_page(Backends.from_env(), isbn) once per call, one after another, in one long-lived event loop as the server does, every call with its own ISBN so a cache cannot help: all-answering pages, stock failing, reviews silent, both optional ones failing, pricing failing fast while the catalog is slow, an unknown ISBN, the catalog failing fast, the catalog slow but within its 1 s, and catalog or pricing silent. Timing is calibrated in the same check: hidden/reference (a TaskGroup over the fixture's own client) runs the same calls before and after the agent's tree, and a budgeted case's limit is 400 ms or 1.6 times the reference's median on it (the slower run), whichever is longer; the run is invalid when a discriminating case's limit reaches 85% of what a one-after-another page needs, and the check raises when the reference fails any check. Required: results_correct (every all-answering call returns exactly the expected page, unchanged 0.1 s after it was returned), failures_as_specified (the page with stock or reviews null, BookNotFound with the ISBN, PageUnavailable naming catalog or pricing as the exception itself rather than inside a group, the full page for a slow catalog), within_budget (each budgeted case's median within its limit, none at the driver's 5 s call limit), no_leaked_work (0.1 s after each call returned or raised, no task it created still pending, no backend request it made still in progress or answered later, none started after it). Measures: per-case medians and limits, the reference's and the sequential floor for the all-answering and pricing-down cases, leaked tasks and requests, pages changed after return, requests hung up, ExceptionGroups raised, the fixture's 16 tests against the agent's package, the agent's own suite, commits. Needs bubblewrap and python3 3.11 or later at /usr/bin; agent arms need nothing extra readable. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: The book page call (`GET /books/{isbn}`) is the slowest thing in the new app: about 850 ms in staging, and the app team's budget for it is 400 ms, after which the app gives up and shows its fallback screen. Could you get it under that? Nothing about the response should change, including what happens when a backend misbehaves: an ISBN the catalog doesn't know is a 404, it's a 503 naming catalog or pricing when either of those can't answer, and stock and reviews come back null when they fail or are slow. When catalog or pricing is down, send the 503 as soon as we know, the way it already does when the catalog is down. The page is built in storefront/book_page.py, and docs/services.md says what each backend does.
